Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prep materials for our internal procurement and product teams, Legal asked whether you can provide a couple of short, public-facing pieces we can reuse in procurement docs and in the console. Specifically:  

- A 1–2 line "what we collect / why" blurb suitable for a sales one-pager and the Hosted API console privacy modal.
- A short, plain-English explanation of how Redwood handles subprocessors and cross-border transfers (we want something we can link to from our procurement packet).

We've attached a quick template and a CSV of the subprocessors we currently need to align for. If you can send back a proposed blurb and a suggested location in the console (e.g., "privacy modal > data transfers" or a footer link), that would help speed procurement sign-off.

Appreciate quick turnaround — procurement is hoping to finalize language by COB Monday.

Best,
Jordan Ramos
Senior Security Counsel | Acme Payments

Plan:
1) Kimberly will propose two short blips: a sales-friendly one-liner and a console-friendly modal paragraph.
2) Laura/Vanessa will flag the best console location and UI copy constraints (character limits, link targets).
3) I'll return a single doc with both options + a short subprocessor explanation and suggested link targets by Monday morning PT.

Two quick clarifications:
- Is Acme OK with a console link that points to a public subprocessor map (hosted on our docs site) rather than embedding the full CSV?
- For cross-border wording, do you prefer referencing the specific legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy decisions) or a higher-level "safeguards" phrasing? Legal's preference will guide the level of technical detail.

Thanks — will be back shortly with concrete language.

Subject: Re: Plain-language DPA snippets for Hosted API

Marcus — drafting below. I kept two tiers: (A) short sales-friendly blurb and (B) slightly longer console modal paragraph with link targets. Also added a short subprocessor explanation intended for procurement. Happy to redline.

(A) Sales one-liner (1 sentence, plain language):
"Redwood processes only the data you send us to power API requests; we do not use your data to train models and we limit access to authorized personnel and subprocessors."

(B) Console modal paragraph (2–3 short sentences):
"Redwood processes customer API requests to provide inference and related services. We do not use customer request data to improve model training, and we retain content only as needed to provide the service and meet contractual obligations. A current list of subprocessors and the legal mechanisms we rely on for cross-border transfers (e.g., SCCs, adequacy) are published here: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/subprocessors."

(Procurement-friendly subprocessor blurb):
"Subprocessors: We maintain a public, regularly updated subprocessor list and provide advance notice for material changes. Where cross-border transfers are necessary, we rely on appropriate safeguards (standard contractual clauses or other valid mechanisms) and offer contractual commitments through our DPA. For specific evidence (SOC reports, data flow diagrams), please let us know and we'll coordinate via your procurement contact."

Notes / legal flags:
- Mentioning SCCs by abbreviation is OK here but avoid deep legal definitions in public text; link to a short legal appendix for customers who need details.
- Avoid implying infinite retention; use "only as needed" language.
- We should not promise specific certification timelines (e.g., "SOC 2 within X") in public copy.

I'm attaching a doc with redlines and a slightly more concise alternate for marketing. Once Laura confirms the console character limits I can trim.

Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Marcus — this is great, thanks. A couple quick notes from Acme Legal and Privacy:  

- The sales one-liner works well for our procurement one-pager.
- For the console modal, we prefer calling out "Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)" in parenthesis on the first pass, to make the mechanism explicit for reviewers who will escalate to our international privacy team. Adding the parenthetical doesn't require additional legal text in the modal itself.
- We would like the public link to be the subprocessor map (not the CSV). The map is fine as long as it includes dates of last update.

Can you confirm you'll point the modal link to the hosted subprocessor map and include a "last updated" timestamp on that page? If so, Procurement can mark this as cleared and push the contract forward.

Thanks again for moving quickly.

—Jordan
Jordan Ramos
Senior Security Counsel | Acme Payments
